chapter_title: The Interpretation [of] the S[i]lence, the Fast, [the Peace], the Day, [and] the Rest; [what] they are.
chapter_note: This chapter is largely an interpretive apparatus mapping named church “lessons” (silence/fast/peace/day/rest) onto cosmological archetypes. That mapping move (ritual term → cosmic entity) is later than the oldest substrate, but several paragraphs preserve clear cosmological fragments (First Man, ship of living waters, great aeon, Pillar of Glory). Frame material appears at the opening (disciples’ request) and in a brief doxological close.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue frame with disciples questioning the enlightener; request/imploring formula and topic-setting list of ritual “lessons” identifies editorial/hagiographic apparatus rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] the gatherer in [... ...] [...] is the Pill[a]r of Gl[or]y [...] because [...] ⟨p.47⟩ [...] up to the [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ethical/practice-facing interpretation about restraining “the body” and “all the lusts of the world … in righteousness,” which reads as a ritual/moral application rather than cosmos→cosmos description. What remains is the cosmological identification with the Pillar of Glory (and related fragmentary causal rationale).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core signal: the Pillar of Glory (a fixed Manichaean cosmic transport/column of Light). Mixed because the surviving middle clause appears to apply the notion to bodily lusts/discipline (institutional-ritual interpretation of “fast”), even though it is preserved only in fragments.

paragraphs.core_text: the [Fi]rst [M]an who dwel[ls i]n the ship of living waters [...] li]ght [...] he is c[alled ...] that they have [...] glorious [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the applicative label-introduction: “The one they call […] it is …” (the move that equates a named, proclaimed ‘lesson’ in the world with a cosmic being).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological exposition survives cleanly once the introductory identification formula is stripped: First Man + ship of living waters is internal to the cosmic system. The initial ‘they call …’ indicates later interpretive mapping from ritual term to archetype.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] uni]verse as they shall [...] in the great aeon [...] are spread in the universe, it is [...] established in the [...] and the so[u]ls [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue/attribution + naming hook: “[…] the enlighten[er … cal]l it ‘day’ […]” which functions as an editorial bridge from cosmology to a ritual term (“day”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core markers: “great aeon,” universe-spread/establishment language, and souls in a cosmic setting. Mixed because the surviving lead-in explicitly frames the description as an interpretation of what is called “day,” i.e., ritual term → cosmological referent.
Beatitude/doxological closure (“Blessed is he… remains for ever and ever”) is characteristic of editorial/hymnic wrapping rather than systematic cosmological mapping.
